title: Latency Safety Lens for Cache & Batch Configuration
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
Design a compact, inspectable "Latency Safety Lens" card to live in the Redwood Console's Caching & Batching configuration panel. The lens helps engineers understand the latency implications and safety guardrails of toggling cache and batching presets before applying them. It must be lightweight, actionable, and able to simulate cost/latency tradeoffs across three representative workload archetypes (conversational, single-shot synth, and bulk-embedding).

Goals:
- Surface expected latency bands (p50/p95/p99) when enabling a given batching/cache preset and quantify the likely increase or decrease in tail latency.
- Explain why a preset changes latency (e.g., longer queue delays for higher batch size vs. reduced per-token compute via caching).
- Provide clear guardrails and safe defaults; show an automated fallback recommendation when latency SLOs would be violated.
- Offer a lightweight simulation with a single-click toggle to preview cost estimate delta and sample request traces.

Design decisions & rationale:
- Compact card driven by three visual elements: (1) latency band sparkline with p50/p95/p99 overlays, (2) quick explanation pill (one-line reason + confidence), (3) action row (preview simulation, apply preset, opt into conservative fallback). This avoids overwhelming the console while giving immediate signal.
- Use a banded sparkline (not heatmap) to communicate variability; the band fills from p50 to p99 with a small dot for median. We chose bands to make tail risk obvious at small sizes.
- Confidence score computed from recent telemetry for matched model/version/hw combination. Show textual caveat when telemetry is low.
- Simulation runs client-side with a learning-enabled cost estimator endpoint for accuracy; results are cached and stamped to the UI.

Prototype & artifacts:
- Figma prototype (iteration v3): https://www.figma.com/file/REDWOOD-Labs/latency-safety-lens-v3
- Conservative microcopy doc (Design Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/redwood-console-microcopy-lens
- Simulation API spec (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/BatchCache+Simulation+API+Spec

Acceptance criteria:
- Card renders correctly in the Caching & Batching panel on desktop widths >= 1000px and collapses to a summary row on mobile/compact consoles.
- Latency band visualization correctly maps to the simulator output (visual vs numbers match within 5%).
- When a preset would push p95 above configured SLO, the card surfaces a red guardrail state with an automated fallback suggestion.
- Clicking Preview runs a simulation and shows cost delta, estimated throughput change, and three sample synthetic traces without blocking the primary config flow.
- Design tokens and colors conform to console theming and pass contrast checks (WCAG 2.1 AA).

Review feedback captured so far:
- PM (Liam Park) asked to include an explicit expected-cost-per-10000-requests figure — added to the preview panel as a small stat.
- Infra lead (Rhea Kapoor) requested the tooltip include model-variant mapping when kernel selection could affect latency (done).
- Eng reviewer (Samir Patel) recommended moving confidence calculation into the backend and returning a telemetry_age field; updated API spec to include telemetry_age.
- Accessibility reviewer (Claire Nguyen) asked that the sparkline bands be navigable with keyboard and announced as "median, 95th percentile at X ms" — added ARIA labels to prototype.

Trade-offs considered:
- We debated full interactive workload simulation versus a lightweight estimator. Full sim is more accurate but adds latency to the UI; the team chose a hybrid approach (fast estimator + optional deep sim in background).
- Showing too many metrics (latency percentiles, cost, throughput, error rate) risks cognitive overload; scoped to latency + cost + simple trace samples for first iteration.

Engineering notes & hooks:
- Simulation endpoint: POST /api/console/v1/simulate-cache-batch with payload {preset_id, model, seq_stats, workload_profile}. Response: {p50, p95, p99, cost_delta, confidence, telemetry_age}. (See Confluence link above.)
- Frontend feature flag for controlled rollout: feature_flag.console.latency_safety_lens.
- Telemetry required: sample window default 24h, fallback to model-family profile if insufficient samples.

Rollout & telemetry plan:
- Rollout via progressive feature flag: 10% (internal), 25% (beta customers), 100% (GA) over 6 weeks.
- Success metrics: adoption_rate (preview clicked / lens shown), apply_rate (preset applied after preview), mean_time_to_revert (if any), and customer-reported regressions. Target apply_rate >= 18% for early adopters.

QA checklist:
- Visuals align with Figma for all breakpoints.
- Simulator results consistent with offline estimator for three canonical workloads.
- Keyboard navigation and screen-reader announcements validated.
- Feature flag toggling shows/hides the card without console reload.

Open questions & next steps:
- Should the card link directly to rollout guardrails for Dedicated clusters? (PM follow-up).
- Add an optional developer mode that surfaces raw request batching metrics for SREs. (Backlog).
- Finalize wording for fallback modal to avoid accidental disabling of batching in high-throughput customers.

Related PRs and artifacts:
- Draft UI PR (frontend): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/6782
- Backend simulation stub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3221

Owner notes:
This ticket is primarily a design deliverable with a small frontend prototype. Engineering will own the simulation endpoint and the confidence telemetry hook. We should aim for a crisp v1 that reduces risk for customers experimenting with aggressive batch/cache presets while keeping the path to deeper simulation and more metrics open for v2.
